subject: Meteorology
title: Giant Hail
description: A quick win: understand Giant Hail.

hook.text: The largest hailstone on record in the US fell in South Dakota in 2010—20 cm across, nearly as big as a volleyball.

buildup.text: Giant hail requires updrafts exceeding 50 m/s—fast enough to support stones weighing nearly a kilogram.

discovery.text: Hail causes billions of dollars in damage annually—shredding crops, denting cars, and smashing roofs.

twist.text: Hail can fall at over 160 km/h—arriving with the kinetic energy of a baseball pitched by a professional.

climax.text: Dual-pol radar can now distinguish hail from rain—giving earlier warnings for the most damaging stones.

punchline.text: Ice balls the size of softballs falling from the sky—nature's fastball.

quiz.question: How large was the record US hailstone from 2010?
